about: theory_marg results (27 Oct 2026). Every entry: value(s), definition, source file, status word.

telescoping_and_parts.definition: Delta_s(j)=LSE_k lam_s(j,k)-LSE_k lam_{s-1}(j,k); naive N_s(j)=sum_i log mean_k P(o_si|j,k); within W_s=log mean_k prod_i P(o_si|j,k)-N_s; memory M_s=Delta_s-N_s-W_s; all centred over j; additive share = Cov(part,Delta)/Var(Delta) pooled over (episode,goal,step); var_ratio = Var(part)/Var(Delta); held-out pool episodes 54000-59999, both latents as goal

persistence_ladder.definition: exact posteriors of models in which the other latent is redrawn per bit (naive), per step (block_1), per block of b steps, once per bit (bit_persistent), never (Bayes); ADF = factorised filter; fixed_policy_* = Gibbs identity with a frozen within-row policy on Bayes lambda_T (Jensen bound). Held-out pool 54,000-59,999, both latents as goal.

fixed_components.definition: episode mean of each rule's centred goal log-belief per goal value (profile), its SD over values (nats) and its share of the total variance, t = 1, 5, 10, 30

structure.definition: V: soft_roll fitted by a cos(om r)+b sin(om r); x two-ridge: 0.5 A^2 [cos(om(j-k)-(th0-th1)) + cos(om(j+k)-(th0+th1))] with mean amplitude and linear phase; harmonics: least squares on cos/sin of 2pi(m z0 + n z1), |m|,|n|<=M, R^2 on held-out z pairs (pool z law); marginal: goal r0, targets centred over j, R^2 on held-out samples of the data law; pattern_table_only = z-independent table E[.|o,j] (z-consistency); per_bit_additive = sum_i g_i(o_i, z_i0, z_i1) with harmonics |m|,|n|<=M per bit and bit value

count_window.definition: within-environment R^2 = 1 - sum((y-ybar_env)-(yhat-yhatbar_env))^2 / sum((y-ybar_env)^2), y = n_{T-1} (5 counts), 400 environments x 40 episodes, pool z law
count_window.reference: R1-e5 linear decoder of n_{T-1} from u_T: within-environment R^2 0.87 (c5_count_rule); innovation R^2 by lag 0..8: 0.87 0.62 0.18 0.11 0.08 0.055 0.033 0.016 0.006 (f4_window_decode)

one_layer_span.definition:
c3: what per-step functions does a SHARED LINEAR read-out get from one layer of ReLU features of [o_t; z]?
(CPU, least squares; nothing trained by gradient.)  Successor of a7_span.py (never run in the first pass).
Feature sets h(o, z) (1000 units unless stated), each followed by a shared least-squares read-out (+ constant):
  stored read-ins: R1 (reservoir_ctx_2), R1-e5, the trained LSTM's read-in, the 5/5 rescue's 5-layer read-in (its last
  ReLU output, the reservoir's input); random ReLU features at PyTorch default init (widths 1000 / 4000: z enters weakly);
  random ReLU features with z-weights scaled to the cosines' scale (w_z ~ N(0, 4^2), o-weights N(0,1), bias U(-4, 4);
  widths 1000 / 4000 / 8000).
Targets per step (fresh z of the pool's training environments 0-53,999; uniform cell; o drawn from it):
  N = naive part, W = within-step part, f = step-wise marginal log-likelihood (both latents as goal, centred per latent,
  20 outputs), joint = the per-step joint evidence (100 outputs, centred over cells).
Held-out R^2 on z of environments 54,000-59,999. Summed rule: the fitted per-step function summed over the 30 steps of the
6,000 held-out pool episodes; accuracy for both latents as goal (f-fit: argmax per latent; joint-fit: row/column LSE).
In the linear-response regime a marginal ESN's per-step contribution is a shared linear combination of its read-in features
(window theorem f), so these numbers bound what one ReLU layer offers a shared linear read-out per step.

projection_test.definition:
c5: how many principal directions of R1-e5's summed state S does its own read-out need?  Held-out accuracy (T=30) of
R1-e5's stored marginal read-out applied to S projected on the top-K eigen-directions of S's uncentred second moment
(training episodes 0-11,999 of the D_critic esn pool; held out 24,000-29,999).  Decides K for the read-out fits c1/c4.

marginal_readout_convexity.definition:
c1 (final version): can a prior trap a MARGINAL read-out on fixed features?  (CPU, read-out only, R1-e5's frozen states.)
Features: R1-e5's per-step LSTM outputs u_t (D_critic pool u_esn_2.npy, one fresh environment per episode; episodes
0-11,999 train, 24,000-29,999 held out), S_t = cumsum u_t, ROTATED onto the top K = 512 eigen-directions of the uncentred
second moment of S (X_t = V_K^T S_t, no rescaling; R1-e5's own read-out keeps 0.425 of its 0.426 held-out accuracy there,
c5_projection_test). Earlier versions (all 1000 directions whitened; top 256 / 128 whitened) were stopped (c1_old_stopped_*):
whitening let Adam over-fit, or the projection lost R1's read-out directions (K = 128: 0.318).
Read-out: goal block of Y_t = W X_t + t c (W 20 x 512, c 20), per-latent softmax.
Losses: 'own' (the networks' SANITY loss: soft clip 1e-3, per-value symmetric KL, minus batch min + 1e-8, power 0.5, mean)
and 'goalCE' = KL(Bayes goal marginal || network), every step.
Part A (convexity, goalCE): full-batch L-BFGS (strong Wolfe) on the WHITENED top-512 coordinates (each direction divided
by its RMS) with a small ridge 1e-4 * ||W||^2 / 2 (a first L-BFGS try on the unwhitened rotation had not converged after
318 evaluations, gradient norm 0.18, and over-fitted: train goalCE 0.74 vs held-out 0.93), from four inits: zero; default (nn.Linear init in R1's
coordinates, rotated); r1own (R1-e5's stored read-out, rotated); prior30 (W = 0, c = 15 v, v = +1 on 5 random values and -1
on the other 5 of each latent: a fixed table with a 30-nat step-1 gap, every disfavoured value below the soft-clip floor).
Part B (the networks' optimiser): Adam lr 1e-3 (constant, as the networks), eps 1e-8, batch 2000 x 30 steps, 1,500 updates,
loss 'own' from zero / r1own / prior12 (kappa 6) / prior30, and goalCE from prior30 and zero. For prior inits: share of
disfavoured (episode, value) pairs with q < 1e-3 at t = 1, 30; mean bias gap; sqrt(v_hat) of the disfavoured biases.
Part C: loss along segments between end points (max excess over the chord; > 0 violates convexity).
Part D: one-dimensional 'own' terms in the logit difference (non-convexity).

marginal_start_readout.definition:
c4: the start state as a 'prior' for the MARGINAL ESN, read-out only.  (CPU; forward passes of R1-e5 + read-out fits.)
R1-e5 (sanity/reservoir_ctx_2_e5: read-in Linear(15->1000)+ReLU, frozen LSTM-1000, marginal read-out) is re-run on the
D_critic pool's episodes (meta_esn_2.npz: fresh environment per episode; train 0-11,999, held out 24,000-29,999) with three
start states (h0, c0): 'native' (R1-e5's stored STM, LTM; checked against the pool's stored u_t), 'zero', and
'episode_random' (an independent N(0,1) draw of h0 and of c0 for every episode, not trainable; seed 7).
For each: ||M_1||_1 (episode mean of u_1, L1 over units), the episode-independent share of u_s (||mean u_s||^2 / mean ||u_s||^2),
and the read-out-only marginal optimum under goalCE (convex; summed logits W S_t + t c, goal block, per-latent softmax),
found by full-batch L-BFGS from zero on S projected on the top-512 eigen-directions of that variant's own S and whitened there,
with ridge lambda * ||W||^2 / 2 for lambda in {1e-4, 1e-3, 1e-2} (as c1 part A; with 1e-4 alone the goalCE optimum
over-fits the 12,000 training environments: c1 part A from zero, train goalCE 0.67 vs held-out 1.00, accuracy 0.32);
reported per lambda and for the lambda with the lowest held-out goalCE.
Also: R1-e5's own stored read-out applied to each variant's states (no refit).

within_env_bit_degree.definition:
c6: inside one environment, how much of the within-step part W (and of the step-wise target f) is linear in the 5 bits
and how much is interaction among bits?  (CPU, exact enumeration of the 32 bit patterns; nothing trained.)
For 3,000 environments (z of pool episodes 0-2,999) and goal latent r0 (r1 is the same by symmetry): for every pattern o,
f(j;o) = log mean_k prod_i P(o_i|j,k,z) (centred over j), N(j;o) = sum_i log mean_k P(o_i|j,k,z) (centred), W = f - N.
Within each environment, weighted least squares of each table (10 values x 32 patterns) on [1, o_1..o_5] with weights
w(o) = P(o|z) (patterns drawn from a uniform cell = the data law): the fit is the 'degree <= 1' (count-linear) part, the
residual the interaction part (degree >= 2 under that law). Shares are of the data-law variance pooled over environments.
A count-linear rule dedicated to one environment can use the degree<=1 part; no count-linear rule can use the interaction
part. Also: the share of W's degree<=1 part that a SHARED per-bit additive function captures is ~0 (a2: W R^2 0.0005).

marginal_entropy_readout.definition:
c7: an entropy bonus on a MARGINAL read-out of R1-e5's frozen states (read-out only).  (CPU.)
Same features and fitting as c4 ('native' start: the D_critic esn pool's stored u_t; episodes 0-11,999 train,
24,000-29,999 held out; S projected on its top-512 eigen-directions and whitened there; ridge 1e-3 * ||W||^2 / 2),
objective goalCE - beta * mean_{e,t} H(q_goal), q_goal = the read-out's goal marginal; beta in {0, 0.003, 0.01, 0.03, 0.1};
full-batch L-BFGS from zero. Reports held-out T=30 / t=10 accuracy, held-out goalCE, 'own', and the mean goal entropy at
T=30 (Bayes's own mean goal entropy at T=30 for reference). Prediction (notes 4(iii)): accuracy within +-0.02 of beta = 0.

marginal_start_ownrefit.definition:
c8: the start state as a 'prior' for the MARGINAL ESN, read-out only, with the networks' own loss (CPU).
R1-e5 re-run on the D_critic esn pool's episodes (train 0-11,999, held out 24,000-29,999) with three start states:
'native' (stored STM, LTM), 'zero', 'episode_random' (independent N(0,1) h0 and c0 per episode, seed 7), as c4.
For each, R1-e5's own read-out (W 20 x 1000, c 20, on the full summed state S_t, no projection) is (a) applied as is and
(b) re-fitted with the networks' loss 'own' (Adam lr 1e-3 for 1,000 updates, then cosine to 1e-5 over 500; eps 1e-8;
batch 2000 x 30 steps; fp32) starting from R1-e5's read-out: the nearest 'own'-optimum of each variant's states.
c4 gives the goalCE optima (which are far less accurate than R1's own read-out: 0.30-0.32 vs 0.425 on native states),
so this is the comparison at R1's own operating point. Prediction (notes 4(iii)): episode_random within -0.03..+0.01 of
native after refit; zero within +-0.02 of native (start 0 gave R1 nothing in full training).

marginal_target_test.definition:
c9: is the depth-1 MARGINAL per-step learner slow because its Bayes target is unreachable (misspecification noise)?
(CPU, 3 threads; mem_harness imported read-only: generator, references, MemNet, losses.)
Three identical memoryless marginal nets (MemNet depth 1, width 1000, out 20; PyTorch default init with the same seed),
trained on the SAME fresh-environment batches (batch 2000, Adam lr 1e-3, eps 1e-8, loss 'own' = the networks' loss)
toward three different goal-marginal targets at every step:
  bayes : Bayes's goal marginal (the networks' target; = run_marginal e2e m1),
  step  : the step-wise rule's cumulative goal marginal (softmax over values of sum_s log mean_k P(o_s|j,k)),
  naive : naive's cumulative goal marginal.
Each target is the exact posterior of a model in which the other latent persists for the whole episode (bayes), for one
step (step) or for one bit (naive); 'naive' is representable by a depth-1 per-step net, 'step' only partly.
Held-out: 8,000 fixed episodes (mem_harness cache, seed 20261027): goal accuracy at T = 30 against the TRUE value, and
agreement of the network's T=30 answer with its own target rule's answer.
Prediction (notes, open item 8, written before running): the naive-target net reaches naive's accuracy (~0.45) by 5k
updates, faster than the bayes-target net; the step-target net learns at least as fast as the bayes-target net.

random_start_offset.definition:
c10: is a per-episode random start a random per-episode PRIOR for the marginal ESN?  (CPU, forward passes only.)
R1-e5 on 3,000 pool episodes (D_critic esn pool, 24,000-26,999), run twice on identical observations: with its native
(trained, shared) start state and with an independent N(0,1) start per episode. With R1-e5's own read-out, the goal-logit
difference D_t = Y_t(random) - Y_t(native) (centred over the 10 goal values) is the random start's contribution.
Reported per step t: RMS of D_t; the fraction of D_t that is constant after the transient (corr of D_t with D_30);
RMS of the native logits' episode-dependent part (centred over values, minus the episode mean); and the accuracy change.
If D_t settles to a fixed per-episode vector of size comparable to the evidence part, the random start acts as a random
prior over the goal values redrawn every episode.

marginal_entropy_own_adam.definition:
c11: entropy bonus on a MARGINAL read-out with the networks' loss and optimiser (matched to run_joint A3's design:
read-out from zero, loss 'own' - beta * mean_{e,t} H(goal marginal), Adam lr 1e-3, eps 1e-8). CPU.
Features: R1-e5's frozen states, as c1 Part B (S projected on its top-512 eigen-directions, unwhitened; train pool
episodes 0-11,999, held out 24,000-29,999); batch 2000 x 30 steps; 1,500 updates (CPU budget; c1 Part B: from zero 'own'
reaches 0.295 at 1,500 and is still rising), beta in {0, 0.03, 0.1}; same batches for all betas.
Question: does an entropy bonus change the marginal read-out's accuracy, as it changes the joint read-out's
(run_joint A3: 0.454 -> 0.585 / 0.593 at beta 0.03 / 0.1)?  Prediction (notes 4(ii)): no (within +-0.02).

external_results_used.note: numbers read from other agents' folders for the predictions-vs-results comparison (their definitions apply); see notes.md section 6
external_results_used.run_esn: learn4/run_esn/results.json and out/*.json (an1 increments, an2 gates, an3 windows, an4 lesions, an5 fixed logits, ro_A/ro_B read-outs)
external_results_used.run_marginal: learn4/run_marginal/results_runs.json, runs/*/*.json, logs/*.log (e2e_d1_s0, e2e_d2_s0, fit_all, e2e_d1_x)
external_results_used.run_joint: learn4/run_joint/runs/*/metrics.json, logs/A.log (A1, A3 entropy, B2 episode_random)

predictions_v2_scored.note: scored after the results; predictions_v2.json is the unchanged pre-results record

scored.claim: A marginal read-out on frozen features under goalCE is convex in (W, c): from zero, PyTorch default init, and a deliberately 'prior-loaded' init (large episode-independent goal-logit table), goalCE read-out training on R1-e5's frozen states ends at the same held-out loss (within 1%) and accuracy (within 0.01). Under 'own' (not convex) the same holds within 0.02 accuracy, except that an init putting goal values below the soft-clip floor (q < 1e-3) in most episodes can slow their recovery.
scored.result: goalCE: L-BFGS from zero/default/R1 read-out/30-nat prior -> one solution (objective 0.683/0.683/0.702/0.683; acc 0.318-0.320; answers agree 96-99%; prior erased). own: 30-nat prior frozen (gap 30.00 after 1,500 Adam updates), 12-nat frozen at 11.6; from zero own is slow (0.295 at 1,500, rising); own non-convex along a segment (+0.092)
scored.verdict: partly: goalCE part confirmed; own-part caveat understated (freeze, not slow recovery); own convergence part untested

scored.claim: At matched updates its acc is within +-0.04 of R1's own from-scratch curve (0.196 / 0.363 / 0.420 at 500 / 5k / 25k; interpolate log-linearly), most likely slightly below it in the first ~2k updates.
